clue.text: Everyone's prepared to back British sport

indicators.note: to back means to come behind, so the other pieces follow the British letter

parts.note: everyone means all; the 's is 'is', a link
game means willing or prepared, as in 'game for anything'

explanation.surface: Everybody is ready to support a British sporting fixture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Everyone's' reads as a possessive, but the 's is just 'is', and 'to back' means coming behind British.
explanation.definitionFit: A ball game is any sport played with a ball, so it is a general term for a sport.

clue.text: Old fortress redesigned as billet

indicators.note: redesigned means the letters of as billet are given a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A historic stronghold has been converted into soldiers' lodgings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'redesigned' rearranges ASBILLET into the Paris fortress-prison stormed in 1789.
explanation.definitionFit: The Bastille was the medieval fortress in Paris used as a state prison, so an old fortress.

clue.text: Landowner, as in rural Dumfriesshire, principally

definitions.text: Landowner, as in rural Dumfriesshire, principally

indicators.note: principally points to the principal, leading, letter of each of the clue's words

explanation.surface: A Scottish property owner, as you would find in the Dumfriesshire countryside.
explanation.walkthrough: The first letters of all five words spell the answer, and the whole clue also describes it: Dumfriesshire is a Scottish county.
explanation.definitionFit: A laird is the Scottish term for a landed proprietor, the owner of an estate.

clue.text: Song title revealing mental state?

parts.note: a well-known song whose title tells us what a singer is thinking about, a US state being in their head; state is a pun on mental state and an American state

explanation.definitionFit: The Hoagy Carmichael standard, famously sung by Ray Charles, names a US state preoccupying the singer's thoughts.

clue.text: Though not hot, sports day official needs a drink

indicators.note: not means the letter for hot is left out of the official

parts.note: a marshal is an official who directs competitors at a sports event
H is the abbreviation for hot, as on taps

explanation.surface: A school sports day steward who is not feeling warm still wants a drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not' removes H from MARSHAL to leave MARSAL, and A is added.
explanation.definitionFit: Marsala is a fortified wine from Sicily, so a type of drink.

clue.text: Composer producing various versions of Hair?

definitions.meaning: Samuel ... was the American composer of the Adagio for Strings
someone who styles hair in different cuts, hair being the musical's title as a misdirection

explanation.walkthrough: Hair is also a famous musical, which makes the second half look like a reference to a composer's arrangements.
explanation.definitionFit: A barber cuts men's hair into various styles, and Samuel Barber was an American composer.

clue.text: British author? All-American, as it turned out

indicators.note: turned out means the letters of all-American and as it are turned into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A supposedly British writer proved to be thoroughly American.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned out' rearranges ALLAMERICANASIT. The question mark warns that 'author' is an example: the Scottish thriller writer of The Guns of Navarone.
explanation.definitionFit: Alistair MacLean was the Scottish thriller novelist, so an example of a British author.

clue.text: Free to enjoy good health outside prison

indicators.note: outside means the phrase for good health goes round the word for free

parts.note: to enjoy good health is to be well
to rid is to free

explanation.surface: Being released lets an inmate thrive beyond the jail walls.
explanation.walkthrough: 'outside' places BE WELL around RID: B(RID)E WELL. Bridewell was a London house of correction whose name came to mean any jail.
explanation.definitionFit: Bridewell, originally a London house of correction, became a general word for a prison or lock-up.

clue.text: A flower held up for monarch

indicators.note: held up, in a down clue, means the letters read from bottom to top

parts.note: a flower is something that flows, a river, here the Niger in West Africa

explanation.surface: A bloom is raised aloft in honour of the queen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'held up' turns A NIGER into REGIN A. 'Flower' as a river is a crossword favourite.
explanation.definitionFit: Regina is Latin for queen, used of a reigning queen, so a monarch.

clue.text: Still hissing

definitions.meaning: the crackling hiss of interference on a radio or recording

explanation.definitionFit: Static means unmoving, and static is also the hissing noise of electrical interference.

clue.text: Cut short journey in part of Ireland

indicators.note: short means the word for cut loses its last letter

parts.note: a slit is a cut
a go can be a turn or trip; to go is to journey

explanation.surface: A truncated trip to a region of Ireland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cut short' looks like one phrase meaning abbreviated, but 'Cut' is the word being trimmed and 'short' is the instruction.
explanation.definitionFit: Sligo is a county and town in the north-west of the Republic of Ireland.

clue.text: Giving details of shopkeeper's daily routine?

definitions.meaning: to retail a story is to recount it in detail
a shopkeeper's daily business is selling goods to the public

explanation.definitionFit: Retail as a verb means to recount in detail, and retail is selling goods to the public in shops.

clue.text: Annoyed, like grandma in international surroundings

indicators.note: surroundings means the abbreviation for international is placed around the other pieces

parts.note: to dig something is slang for liking it
nan is an informal word for grandmother

explanation.surface: Granny is cross when competing in a global sporting event.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Like' is a verb, slang for enjoy, not a comparison; 'surroundings' signals the abbreviation enclosing the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: Indignant means angry at perceived unfairness, so annoyed.

clue.text: Item of clothing with fashionable association

parts.note: a tie is a neck garment worn with a shirt
in means fashionable, as in 'the in thing'

explanation.surface: A garment linked with being stylish.
explanation.definitionFit: A tie-in is a connection or link between things, such as a film and its merchandise.

clue.text: Monk wrong to be included in raunchy dance

indicators.note: to be included in means the word for wrong is placed inside the monk

parts.note: a lama is a Tibetan Buddhist monk
bad means wrong or wicked

explanation.surface: A monk errs by taking part in a sexy dance.
explanation.definitionFit: The lambada is a Brazilian dance famous for close, sensual hip movements.

clue.text: Fruit liqueur, liberal supply imbibed by yours truly

indicators.note: imbibed by means the reworked letters are drunk into the word for the speaker

parts.note: yours truly is a jokey way of saying me, the speaker

indicators.note: supply is read as supple-ly, in a flexible way, so the letters of liberal are bent into a new order

explanation.surface: I drink a generous quantity of a fruity spirit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'supply' is read as 'in a supple way', bending liberal's letters; 'liberal supply' poses as a generous quantity.
explanation.definitionFit: Mirabelle is a small yellow plum and also the clear brandy distilled from it.

clue.text: Cold with frost at a peninsula

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps
rime is hoar frost formed from freezing fog

explanation.surface: Wintry frost arrives at a coastal headland.
explanation.definitionFit: Crimea is a peninsula jutting into the Black Sea.

clue.text: Old railway system is source of trouble in Aussie location

parts.note: BR stands for British Rail, the former national railway in the UK
a bane is a cause of misery or trouble

explanation.surface: An outdated train network is the cause of headaches.
explanation.walkthrough: British Rail ran the UK's trains until privatisation in the 1990s.
explanation.definitionFit: Brisbane is the state capital of Queensland, so a place in Australia.

clue.text: Make trouble initially for former statesman

parts.note: a brand is a make of product

indicators.note: initially means the first letter of trouble is taken

explanation.surface: Stirring up problems is what a past politician did.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Make' is a noun, a brand of goods, not the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Willy Brandt was West German Chancellor and a Nobel peace laureate, so a former statesman.

clue.text: Emperor with brown skin securing power in India

indicators.note: securing means the tanned skin holds the Indian power inside it

parts.note: a tan is skin browned by the sun
the Raj was British rule in India; raj means rule or sovereignty

explanation.surface: A sun-browned ruler holds sway over India.
explanation.definitionFit: Trajan was a Roman emperor of the second century AD.

clue.text: Rose King, novelist

parts.note: R stands for Rex, Latin for king
Eric Ambler was an English writer of spy thrillers

explanation.surface: A monarch and an author named in a list of notable figures.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rose' looks like a verb or a name; it is a climbing rose.
explanation.definitionFit: A rambler is a climbing rose with long flexible shoots, a kind of rose.

clue.text: Person responsible for court case engineers subsequent hearing

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, the British Army's engineering corps

indicators.note: hearing means a word is to be taken by how it sounds when spoken

parts.note: subsequent means later

explanation.surface: Army sappers attend a later court session.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hearing' doubles as a court term, but it signals that LATER is heard as LATOR.
explanation.definitionFit: A relator is a person who brings information on which a legal action is taken, in effect the instigator of a case.

clue.text: Incorporating an extra piano, recorded hit

indicators.note: incorporating an extra means one more letter is taken into the word for recorded

parts.note: taped means recorded on tape
P is the musical abbreviation for piano, softly

explanation.surface: A recording session adds a second piano and produces a hit single.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Incorporating an extra' adds a P inside TAPED. 'Hit' is a verb, a light knock, not a chart success.
explanation.definitionFit: To tap is to strike lightly, so tapped means hit.

clue.text: A bishop introduces foreign ruler in sacred place

parts.note: B is the chess abbreviation for bishop
a bey was a governor in the Ottoman Empire

explanation.surface: A clergyman presents an overseas potentate in a holy building.
explanation.definitionFit: An abbey is a church or monastery building, a consecrated place.

clue.text: Distributes drinks around pub, running short before ""Time"

indicators.note: around means the drinks go round the other pieces

parts.note: ales are beers, drinks

indicators.note: before means the trimmed pub precedes the time letter
running short means the pub word loses its last letter

parts.note: a local is one's neighbourhood pub

explanation.surface: A landlord hands out drinks around the bar as stocks dwindle before closing time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'running short' trims the pub word by its last letter; 'around' then wraps the drinks round that and the time letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To allocate is to share out or apportion, so allocates means distributes.

clue.text: Source of infection among certain tribes

indicators.note: among means the letters sit within the run of certain tribes

explanation.surface: A disease is spreading among some tribal peoples.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across cerTAIN Tribes.
explanation.definitionFit: A taint is a trace of contamination or corruption that spreads, a source of infection.

clue.text: Friend meets mine worker, all of a flutter?

parts.note: a pal is a friend
a pit is a coal mine
an ant is the classic crossword worker, from worker ants

explanation.surface: A pal meets a coal miner and gets nervous.
explanation.definitionFit: Palpitant means palpitating, trembling or throbbing, so in a state of agitation.

clue.text: Priest's talked of by a woman

indicators.note: talked of means the word is taken by its spoken sound

parts.note: Eli was the priest who raised Samuel in the Bible; with the 's it is Eli's

explanation.surface: A clergyman's affairs are gossiped about by a woman.
explanation.walkthrough: Eli's, said aloud, gives ELIZ; A follows.
explanation.definitionFit: Eliza is a woman's name, so it stands for a woman.

clue.text: Is terrified father's about to enter

indicators.note: to enter means the word for about goes into the father's

parts.note: dad is father, and the 's gives dad's
re means about or concerning

explanation.surface: Someone is scared because Dad is about to come in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about to enter' looks like 'soon to enter', but 'about' is the piece and 'to enter' the instruction.
explanation.definitionFit: To dread is to fear greatly, so dreads means is terrified.

clue.text: Cruel fellow has fixed trap for woman with brown hair

indicators.note: has fixed means the cruel fellow holds the trap set within him

parts.note: a brute is a cruel person
a net is a trap for catching animals

explanation.surface: A cruel man has laid a snare for a dark-haired woman.
explanation.definitionFit: A brunette is a woman with dark brown hair.
